extracted.intended_audience: Prospective FY25 MURI grant applicants (universities, companies, non-profits, research teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory terms for preparing proposals and post-award compliance under the DoD FY25 MURI Funding Opportunity Announcement, including topic-specific research scope, certification requirements, reporting obligations, and allowable resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Review Meeting hosting term and cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: [Name of entity] offers the use of its facilities for a DoD Program Review Meeting to discuss the status of programs related to the subject of this proposal. ... No fee will be charged Program Review Meeting attendees. [Name of entity] understands it will not be asked to host a Performance Review Meeting more than once per year, if at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants interested in hosting such meetings should include an estimated cost and the above language in their proposals; language becomes part of any award. Applicants are not required to include the term and omission will not affect selection. If a contract is awarded, use of the facility will be included as an option.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFATA reporting compliance (2 CFR Part 170)
rubrics_metrics.description: All recipients applying for financial assistance must provide information in their proposal that describes the necessary processes and systems in place to comply with reporting requirements identified in 2 CFR Part 170 Appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities are required to meet reporting requirements unless an exception or exemption applies; refer to 2 CFR Part 170 (including Appendix A) for detailed requirements, exceptions, and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Assistance Certification (SF-424 (R&R) block 17; SF-LLL, tax liability, felony disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Financial Assistance Certifications Report attests that the entity will abide by laws, regulations, and supplemental certifications. As applicable, submit documentation including Standard Form-LLL “Disclosure Form to Report Lobbying” and disclosure of any unpaid delinquent tax liability or a felony conviction under any Federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 (R&R) block 17 you agree to comply with Lobbying Disclosure Act (if applicable) and represent you do not have unpaid assessed federal tax liability (with exhausted remedies) and were not convicted of a felony under federal law within preceding 24 months. If you cannot make these representations, you are ineligible unless an SDO determines otherwise; provide information to the agency SDO promptly to permit consideration before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications Regarding Restrictions on Lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: For grant awards >$100,000 applicants must certify: (1) No Federal appropriated funds have been or will be paid to influence federal officials in connection with awards; (2) If non-federal funds were or will be paid for influencing, submit SF-LLL; (3) Include this certification language in award documents for all subawards so subrecipients certify and disclose accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification is a material representation required by 31 U.S.C. 1352; failure to file the required certification may result in civil penalties of not less than $10,000 and not more than $100,000 per failure. Instructions for SF-LLL available at http://www.whitehouse.gov/sites/default/files/omb/grants/sflllin.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on internal confidentiality agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant represents it does not require employees, contractors, or subrecipients to sign or comply with internal confidentiality agreements that prohibit or restrict lawful reporting of fraud, waste, or abuse to designated investigative or law enforcement representatives of Federal departments or agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 (R&R) block 17 you certify to the above; false statements may subject the signer to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (U.S. code, Title 18, Section 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding disclosure of funding sources (Section 223(a) compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 (R&R) block 17, the proposing entity certifies compliance with Section 223(a) of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry NDAA FY2021: (a) PI and key personnel certify current and pending support is current, accurate and complete; (b) agree to update disclosures at agency request prior to award and as requested during award term; (c) PI and key personnel have been made aware of these requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False, fictitious, or fraudulent statements may subject the signer to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (U.S. code, Title 18, Section 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest disclosure (2 CFR 200.318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must comply with 2 CFR 200.318(c) Codes of Conduct to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in award administration; disclose any potential or actual scientific or nonscientific conflict(s) of interest for the applicant, organization, and any identified subrecipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include collaborators (even if they did not formally provide support) in list of current and pending support. The agency may request additional information and may require an approved conflict of interest mitigation plan after application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to comply with 2 CFR 200.318(c), Codes of Conduct, to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in award administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision will be incorporated into all assistance instruments awarded under this FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review participation and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals funded as basic research, DoD may utilize peer reviewers from academia, industry, and government to periodically appraise performance; peer reviewers who are not U.S. Government employees must sign nondisclosure agreements before receiving proposal copies or reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviews monitor quality and help determine continued DoD funding. Applicants may include travel costs for PI to attend peer review. Peer reviews may consider information from project or program review meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on procurement of foreign-made Unmanned Aircraft Systems (COTS UAS) and waiver rules
rubrics_metrics.description: COTS UAS may not be purchased pursuant to this grant/contract/prototype until a waiver per DoD memorandum (May 23, 2018) is obtained by the cognizant DoD Program Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver is not required when research is via a grant, unclassified, funded with basic (6.1) or applied (6.2) research funds and performed on campus by a university. Waivers are required for other grants/assistance agreements and for all contract awards/other transaction agreements. Waivers are required regardless of award type when interactions involve military personnel, DoD property/facilities, government labs/UARCs/FFRDCs, PAO, classified work, or exploration of specific military utility; in such cases a Cyber Security waiver or ATO and Cyber Vulnerability Assessment must be obtained. Prospective/current performers must notify the DoD Program Officer of anticipated COTS UAS purchases at white paper/proposal time or for award changes, provide documentation (type, effort, location, etc.), cooperate with requests to support the waiver and Cyber Vulnerability Assessment, and must not expend federal funds or make purchases subject to a waiver until formally notified that requirements have been met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient Integrity & Performance reporting (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII; SAM/FAPIIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Federal share of any award includes more than $500,000 over performance period, the Award Term and Condition for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII) applies. If a recipient's currently active federal awards exceed $10,000,000 at any time during the award period, the recipient must maintain currency of information reported to SAM/FAPIIS about civil, criminal, or administrative proceedings as described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is statutory under 41 U.S.C. 2313. Information posted in the integrity/performance system is publicly available (except past procurement performance reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings to report under integrity/performance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must report proceedings that: (a) are in connection with federal awards; (b) reached final disposition during the most recent five-year period; and (c) are: 1) criminal proceedings resulting in conviction; 2) civil proceedings resulting in finding of fault and payment of monetary fine/penalty/restitution/damages of $5,000 or more; 3) administrative proceedings resulting in finding of fault and payment of monetary fine/penalty of $5,000 or more or reimbursement/restitution/damages in excess of $100,000; or 4) any other proceeding that could have led to outcomes in (1)-(3), had a consent/compromise with acknowledgment of fault occurred, and disclosure does not conflict with law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report only proceedings connected to federal award performance. Use SAM Entity Management area to enter required information. No need to submit separately under assistance awards if already reported via SAM for procurement contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting procedures and frequency for integrity/performance matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter required proceedings information in the SAM Entity Management area. Recipients subject to the requirement must report proceedings information through SAM for the most recent five-year period, either reporting new proceedings or affirming no new information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients with cumulative federal contract, grant, and cooperative agreement awards >$10,000,000 must disclose semiannually any information about criminal, civil, and administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative proceeding: non-judicial adjudicatory process to determine fault or liability (e.g., SEC administrative proceedings, CBCA, ASBCA). Conviction: judgment/conviction of a criminal offense by any court of competent jurisdiction, including nolo contendere. Total value of currently active awards: includes only the Federal share of awards with recipient cost share and value of expected funding increments and options even if not yet exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions clarify which proceedings and award values must be considered for reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award reporting requirements and formats (agency-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR, ARO, and AFOSR have post-award reporting requirements and specific instructions/forms: ONR addendum page for DoD R&D General Terms; ARO Form 18 'Reporting Instructions'; AFOSR uses Federal-wide RPPR for interim, annual, and final reports and submission portals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links provided for detailed submission and formatting instructions. A Federal-wide RPPR is under development; performers do not have to use RPPR now but DoD plans future use and may issue award modifications requiring RPPR after Federal Register notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 1 objective and research concentration areas (Superatom-based materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: Identify interactions that control novel transport properties in superatom-based materials and develop understanding to design, synthesize, and characterize these materials and create design rules to guide optimization and explore uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested research areas include (1) characterization of novel properties (electronic and spin transport) to identify coherent transport mechanism; (2) theoretical/computational methods and design rules to predict/optimize transport and guide synthesis; (3) synthesis of novel materials based on nanoscale building blocks; (4) exploration of other novel properties and possible uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 1 anticipated resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated awards under Topic 1 will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 7 funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chief during the white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 2 objective and research concentration areas (Moiré-engineered oxide bicrystals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: Elucidate fundamental structures and physics, locally and over distance, of bicrystalline oxides formed by Moiré engineering, including engineered interfaces and free surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research foci include (1) processing to produce suitable membranes (control composition, thickness, termination); (2) nanoscale structural and chemical studies (e.g., electron microscopy, local spectroscopy); (3) mapping of strain fields; (4) first-principles modeling of nanoscale structure and local properties; (5) mesoscale modeling relating periodic structures to selected electronic, magnetic, and optoelectronic properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 2 anticipated resources
rubrics_metrics.description: This topic requires an investment of $1.5M per year for five years, supporting up to seven funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact topic chiefs for clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 3 objective and research concentration areas (Energy and information processing in biological organisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: Support investigations of relationships between energy consumption and information processing in biological organisms to identify strategies relevant for human and computer performance in energy-constrained environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should bring multidisciplinary expertise (biology, neuroscience, biophysics, biochemistry, information theory, etc.), consider energetic requirements across scales (cellular to integrated systems), and explicitly specify their definition and associated measures of information appropriate for their research questions. Suggested concentration areas include: (1) biological information-processing strategies trading energy for graceful degradation; (2) factors impacting metabolic/energetic cost of an information bit; (3) predictions from biophysically-realistic models; (4) implications for human perceptual and cognitive performance under caloric restrictions; (5) information theory-based computational strategies for energy-constrained artificial systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 3 anticipated resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards under this topic are anticipated to be no larger than $1.5M per year for five years and fund no more than six faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase.
